title: Consolidated request skill matrix and automated routing for console/reporting asks
creator: Mariana Lopez
description:
Problem: Enterprise and mid-market customers repeatedly submit heterogeneous console/reporting asks (ad hoc exports, tenant-level cost breakdowns, custom dashboards). The current triage is manual, slow, and inconsistent across squads, causing long lead times and missed SLA expectations.

Goal: Build a lightweight, defensible intake + automated routing system that: (1) enriches requests with signals, (2) matches asks to the most qualified team/track via a skill matrix, (3) assigns a priority lane and expected delivery window, and (4) produces a pre-check cost/feasibility summary for PM/Eng reviewers. This reduces manual backlog grooming, standardizes evidence requirements, and speeds response for high-impact customers.

Scope: Console and reporting requests only (usage analytics, consumption/cost breakdowns, scheduled/tabular exports, ad-hoc dashboards). This ticket covers product definitions, scoring rules, routing matrix, acceptance criteria, and the lightweight UI changes to the intake form. Execution depends on engineering tasks for the API enrichments and backend routing (ENG dependencies listed).
acceptance_criteria: New intake form variant available in Console that collects standardized fields for reporting asks: business goal, desired cadence (one-off/scheduled), sample dataset, expected volume, tenant size, and regulatory flags.
Automated enrichment pipeline attaches 4 signals to incoming asks: tenant tier, estimated rows/GB, related metrics/dashboard IDs, and recent support interactions (requires ENG-41234).

A skill matrix (CSV-managed in product drive) maps common request archetypes to owning squads and fallback lanes; automated routing assigns owner + SLA lane with >85% alignment to manual historical labels in pilot dataset.

Priority scoring engine (weights documented) assigns lanes: Fast Response (48-72h), Scoped Project (2-6 weeks), Enterprise Engagement (sales/solutions handoff) and surfaces a preflight cost estimate for scoped exports.

Console shows a generated summary card for PM/Eng reviewers with: routing rationale, estimated cost (tokens/compute/ETL), and minimum evidence checklist. Reviewers can accept, request more info, or reassign.
Pilot run with 30 historical requests achieves a 60% reduction in manual triage time and preserves customer satisfaction (CSAT target >= 4/5).
notes_updates: 2025-10-12: Created — initial problem writeup and high-level goals after stakeholder workshop (Growth, Sales Eng, Platform PMs).

2025-10-17: Alignment meeting — decided to limit scope to console/reporting asks (exclude instrumentation/observability feature requests). Agreed on three SLA lanes and required evidence items per lane.

2025-10-21: Spike with sample of 150 past tickets: we can extract tenant tier and request archetype from labels 72% of time; missing fields require intake form enforcement. Trade-off: stricter form reduces friction for self-serve customers — we will make additional fields optional for self-serve but required for enterprise-tagged tenants.
2025-10-28: Design review — added summary card UI and quick-action buttons (Accept / Request more info / Escalate to Solutions). UX will hide cost estimate for one-off small exports to reduce noise.

2025-11-01: Engineering sync — ENG-41234 will add new enrichment endpoints; ENG-39876 owns routing microservice changes. Preliminary API contract agreed; data warehouse queries for cost preflight flagged as ENG-42100.
2025-11-02: Decision: Pilot will run for 6 weeks with three support cohorts; success metrics and governance defined below. Next steps created as action items.
additional_considerations: Scoring weights: initial emphasis on customer tier (40%), request complexity estimate (30%), and business impact flagged by Sales (30%). These are adjustable post-pilot.
Privacy: when enriching with support transcripts, strip PII and ensure compliance with tenant data policies; Security team review required (sec_review flag true).
Operationalization: routing decisions must be auditable and exportable for monthly review; maintain a small human-in-loop override path for the first 8 weeks of the pilot.

Fallback behavior: if the assigned squad is >20% overloaded (based on capacity signal from Dedicated autoscaler metrics), route to pool of cross-functional responders and notify product ops. Requires instrumentation from ENG-39876.
Trade-offs: aggressive automation reduces latency but risks misrouted work; conservative thresholds increase manual work. Pilot will iterate thresholds weekly.
next_steps: Finalize intake form fields and validation rules (owner: Design, due 2025-11-09).
ENG: deliver enrichment endpoint (ENG-41234) and routing microservice hooks (ENG-39876) by 2025-11-20.
Define and publish skill matrix CSV and mapping rules (owner: Mariana Lopez, due 2025-11-12).
Run pilot on 3 cohorts (solutions-led, self-serve enterprise, low-touch customers) for 6 weeks and collect triage time, routing accuracy, and CSAT.
Weekly review with PM/Eng/Design for thresholds adjustments; produce stakeholder update 2025-11-16.
